issues.title: How reliable are LLMs at mapping malware/threat behavior to MITRE ATT&CK techniques (TTP mapping)?
open_questions: REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 31 -- the original form ('Does the CTI-ATE F1 ceiling of 0.64 generalize to the newer/larger models evaluated in CyberSOCEval (src-0005, 2025-era)?') was UNANSWERABLE AS POSED and must not be reinstated: cycle 26 established that src-0005 REPORTS NO ATT&CK METRIC AT ALL, so it can never be the comparand. WHAT IS GENUINELY OPEN: no evaluation in this base measures ATT&CK technique extraction on 2026-era frontier models. The two post-2024 measurements that exist are src-0007's (Mar 2026) on GPT-4o and o3-mini, and both land far BELOW src-0002's 0.6388 rather than above it (0.2787/0.2270 and 0.3480/0.1759 precision/recall) -- so there is no evidence of the ceiling rising with model generation, and some evidence against, but the two numbers are not commensurable and cycle 31 established that they are produced under two RADICALLY DIFFERENT and now-known-to-differ scoring rules (see candidate 3). The question a future cycle should actually ask is: does any published evaluation score a 2026-era frontier model on ATT&CK technique extraction under a STATED correctness rule? === CYCLE-45 UPDATE (T2): PARTIALLY ADVANCED BY src-0021, AND IT CARRIES A TRAP THAT WOULD REPRODUCE ctr-0001's DEFECT IF WALKED INTO. === THE ADVANCE, on both limbs of the question as posed. FRONTIER MODELS: src-0021 (TTPrint) evaluates, verbatim, 'GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Gemini 2.5 Flash. Open-source models include Qwen 3 235B and DeepSeek v3.2' -- the first 2026-era frontier backbones in this base to be scored on ATT&CK technique extraction. STATED RULE: it states its metric AGGREGATION verbatim -- 'We evaluate at the document level by aggregating predictions across the full report and comparing the resulting technique set to the ground truth. Final scores are macro-averages over all documents: F1bar = 1/|D| sum_{d in D} F1_d' -- and its LABEL GRANULARITY verbatim, from the prompt, 'Output only ATT&CK technique IDs in parent-technique format: TXXXX, no child technique like TXXXX.XXX'. BUT THE ITEM-LEVEL TP/FP/FN ALGEBRA IS NOT PRINTED: a targeted fetch for the set-intersection formula reported that the paper only references macro-averaged F1 computed per document without showing the underlying precision/recall calculation. So the correctness rule is RECOVERABLE ONLY AS AN INFERENCE from two stated facts (a per-document set comparison over parent-level IDs), NOT as a quoted rule, and this question's literal demand for a STATED correctness rule is therefore ADVANCED BUT NOT SATISFIED. THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS PARAGRAPH EXISTS: src-0021's headline 76.48% and 87.39% macro-F1 ARE SCORES FOR THE TTPrint SCAFFOLD, NOT BARE-LLM SCORES. TTPrint is a multi-stage system -- divergent decomposition into atomic behaviours, a deterministic span-localization stage, then a convergent verification stage retaining 'only candidates supported by both the localized evidence and the authoritative MITRE definition'. SETTING 76.48 OR 87.39 AGAINST src-0002's 0.6388 OR src-0007's 0.2787 REPRODUCES EXACTLY THE SYSTEM-VERSUS-MODEL CONFOUND THAT ctr-0001 WAS OPENED ABOUT for src-0003's LANCE. NO T3 AND NO T4 MAY MAKE THAT COMPARISON. What a model-level comparand requires is the paper's PER-BACKBONE BARE BASELINES, and THOSE WERE NOT CAPTURED AT CYCLE 43 -- capturing that multi-backbone table is the single highest-value unfinished fetch on this source (carry-forward [80]). TWO FURTHER LIMITS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH ANY USE: TTPrint-Bench is an AUTHOR-BUILT BENCHMARK TOPPED BY ITS OWN AUTHORS' SYSTEM and TRAM-Clean is those same authors' cleaning of someone else's benchmark, so the 'outperforming the leading baseline by 63.5%' figure inherits that; and the source is an UNREVIEWED v1 PREPRINT (Comments 'Preprint', no journal reference). NOTE FINALLY THAT src-0020 DOES NOT ADVANCE THIS QUESTION AT ALL: its seven models are open-source only (DeepSeek-V2.5, GPT-OSS 120B and 20B, Llama 3.1 Instruct 70B and 8B, Gemma 3 27B and 12B), and its best micro-F1 of 0.22 MUST NOT be read as evidence about 2026-era frontier capability.

STILL OPEN, TWENTIETH CYCLE MERELY LISTED, AND NOW SHARPENED RATHER THAN DISCHARGED. Is there a human-analyst baseline for ATT&CK technique extraction to contextualize whether these scores are close to human or far below it? NOBODY MAY TREAT src-0018's 41-minutes-per-report figure as discharging this: that is a THROUGHPUT baseline, not an accuracy baseline. Cycle 31 sharpens the question rather than answering it: now that the src-0007/src-0017 scorer's rule is known to be EXACT technique-ID set matching with no partial credit and no parent/sub-technique credit, a useful human baseline would have to be scored under the SAME rule -- and an exact-ID rule is one under which two competent human analysts would themselves disagree substantially, since ATT&CK sub-technique assignment is a known-contested annotation task. So the absence of a human baseline is not merely a gap in this base; it is the reason the absolute magnitudes (0.22-0.35, 0.6388) cannot currently be read as evidence about how hard the task is for anyone. NO SOURCE IN THIS BASE SUPPLIES ONE. === CYCLE-45 UPDATE (T2): ADVANCED, NOT DISCHARGED, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT. === The sentence immediately above -- 'NO SOURCE IN THIS BASE SUPPLIES ONE' -- STILL STANDS, because it is about an ACCURACY baseline. What changed at cycle 43 is that the base acquired, for the first time in twenty-three cycles of this question being merely listed, QUANTITATIVE INTER-ANNOTATOR AGREEMENT for parent-level ATT&CK technique labelling, from TWO INDEPENDENT TEAMS. src-0020, verbatim: 'Following the six-phase process, we reached a mean inter-annotator agreement of kappa=0.68 across 114 techniques (Landis and Koch: substantial agreement [25]), with 65 techniques (57.0%) exceeding the kappa>=0.7 quality threshold.' -- a MEAN over 114 per-technique Cohen's kappa values, reported with NO confidence interval, and with 43% of techniques falling BELOW a kappa>=0.7 bar. src-0021, verbatim: 'Each report carries sentence-level annotations produced under double-annotation with adjudication by 3 qualified annotators, achieving Cohen's kappa=0.76' on TTPrint-Bench, plus kappa=0.74 for 'the pairwise kappa between annotators computed over the set of contested cases' on TRAM-Clean. TWO TEAMS, TWO CORPORA, ONE BAND: 0.68-0.76, 'substantial' on Landis and Koch but well short of the near-perfect agreement an exact-ID scoring rule implicitly presumes. WHAT THIS DOES SETTLE: cycle 31 wrote into this very question that 'ATT&CK sub-technique assignment is a known-contested annotation task' AS A BARE ASSERTION WITH NO SOURCE BEHIND IT. That assertion now has quantitative support -- and the support is in one respect STRONGER than the assertion required, because it was measured on PARENT-level labels, i.e. on the EASIER labelling problem, and trained humans still disagree materially there. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, AND NO CYCLE MAY BLUR IT: AN AGREEMENT STATISTIC IS NOT AN ACCURACY BASELINE. Kappa says two trained annotators disagree with each other; it does not say how well a human scores against a gold standard, so it cannot tell us whether 0.22, 0.2787 or 0.6388 are close to human or far below it -- which is exactly what this question asks. Both papers were checked for a human accuracy or F1 figure at cycle 43 and BOTH ARE ABSENT. THE STANDING PROHIBITION IS UNCHANGED AND IS NOW JOINED BY A SECOND: nobody may treat src-0018's 41-minutes-per-report THROUGHPUT figure as discharging this, and nobody may treat src-0020's or src-0021's KAPPA as discharging it either. WHAT WOULD DISCHARGE IT: a published figure for human-analyst accuracy against a gold standard on ATT&CK technique extraction, ideally scored under a stated rule so that it is commensurable with the machine scores it is meant to contextualise. That remains a T1 collection target and no scheduled task currently reaches it.

PARTIALLY ANSWERED cycle 16, and for the generic case the answer is NO -- fine-tuning made this sub-task WORSE, not better. src-0007's Table 4 gives ATT&CK TTP identification precision/recall of 0.2787/0.2270 for GPT-4o falling to 0.2387/0.1846 for the fine-tuned GPT-4o, and 0.1771/0.1414 for fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini, against 0.3480/0.1759 for o3-mini. This directly matches src-0001's finding that fine-tuning can actively degrade CTI sub-tasks rather than 'partially improve' them. STILL OPEN AS LITERALLY POSED: src-0007's fine-tuning is general task fine-tuning, not fine-tuning specifically on ATT&CK-technique-extraction data, so whether a targeted ATT&CK fine-tune would behave differently is untested by any source in this base. CYCLE 31 ADDS ONE CONSTRAINT ON HOW ANY FUTURE ANSWER MAY BE READ: the released scorer admits a predicted technique ID on the sole condition that the ID appears in its mapping file, and DISCARDS the model's own description of the technique before scoring (candidate 3), so a fine-tune that improved the QUALITY of technique descriptions while leaving ID selection unchanged would register as exactly zero improvement on this metric.

CTI-ATE IS NOT AMONG THEM, the string 'cti-ate' does not occur in the file, and the executable functions are exactly compute_mcq_accuracy, compute_rcm_accuracy, compute_vsp_mad and compute_taa_accuracy. The link is an inference from the artefact being the paper's release, and it must be labelled as such wherever it is used.
