On (b) cycle 31 explicitly RETRACTS its own first two readings -- two fetches reported the mapping as containing only about 57-59 technique IDs ending at T1197, which would have been a spectacular finding, and the file size proves both were FETCH TRUNCATION ARTEFACTS rather than the file. No claim about the mapping's coverage may be made until it is read by some means that does not truncate. CYCLE-32 UPDATE, PARTIAL PROGRESS ON (b) AND NONE ON (a). (b) IS NOW PARTLY ANSWERED IN A WAY THAT DOES NOT REQUIRE THE ROW COUNT: cycle 32 read the HEAD of TTP_Mapping.csv verbatim under an explicit instruction to claim nothing about the whole file, and established its SCHEMA -- header ',TechniqueID,name,longdescription,is sub-technique,sub-technique of,description,tactics', with an is-sub-technique boolean and an explicit parent-ID column, and with parent T1548 and sub-techniques T1548.001 through T1548.005 all present as separate rows. So the mapping demonstrably admits BOTH granularities, which is what the double-penalty consequence in candidate 3 needs, and that consequence no longer depends on the unknown total. THE TOTAL NUMBER OF TECHNIQUE IDS REMAINS UNKNOWN and cycle 31's retraction stands: no cycle may state the mapping's coverage from a fetch, because both of cycle 31's attempts were truncation artefacts and cycle 32's fetch was truncated too, by design. A route that would settle it without fetching the file: the GitHub contents API gives byte size only, so what is actually needed is either a search API query or an unfetched-file line count, and NEITHER HAS BEEN FOUND -- treat this as an infrastructure limit rather than a to-do, subject to the standing caution that such limits deserve one re-test by a genuinely different route. (a) IS COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED AND IS NOW THE MORE IMPORTANT OF THE TWO. Whether the ground-truth ttps fields in data/100-days-articles.json use parent-level technique IDs only, sub-technique IDs, or a mixture, is what determines HOW OFTEN the exact-ID rule double-penalises, and therefore whether the 0.2787/0.2270-class figures are a measurement of technique selection or substantially an artefact of granularity mismatch. That file is 1,441,832 bytes and truncates. TWO CHEAP ROUTES NEITHER CYCLE 31 NOR 32 TRIED, and a future cycle should: stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/example/ is a small directory and may contain a worked article with its ground-truth ttps field intact, and stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/README.md documents a worked two-article example whose ground-truth entries would show the format directly. NOTE ALSO, from the executing code and bearing on how any answer must be read: article_ttps_set is built with the filter 'if " - " in ttp', so any ground-truth entry NOT written in the form 'ID - Name' is silently excluded from the ground truth altogether and can generate neither a true positive nor a false negative -- so the format question is not merely about granularity, it also determines the effective size of the recall denominator.

NEW AT CYCLE 45 (T2), AND IT IS THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT NOW GOVERNS THIS WHOLE ISSUE. THE FOUR ATT&CK MEASUREMENTS IN THIS BASE ARE MUTUALLY NON-COMMENSURABLE, AND ACQUIRING TWO MORE SOURCES AT CYCLE 43 DID NOT PRODUCE TWO MORE COMPARABLE NUMBERS. Laid out so no cycle has to re-derive it: (1) src-0002 CTI-ATE, 0.6388 for ChatGPT-4 -- document/instance level over 60 malware instances and 397 unique techniques, metric AMBIGUOUS between Micro-F1 (body text, one occurrence) and Macro-F1 (Table 1 header, one occurrence), item-level correctness rule UNSTATED and now known to be UNRECOVERABLE from paper and code alike (see open_questions[3]). (2) src-0007 / src-0017, 0.2787 precision / 0.2270 recall for GPT-4o -- EXACT SUB-TECHNIQUE-ID set intersection with NO partial credit and NO parent/sub-technique credit, read off executing code at cycle 31, and with a ground-truth filter ('if " - " in ttp') that silently drops malformed entries from the recall denominator. (3) src-0020, best micro-F1 0.22 -- SENTENCE-level, PARENT-level (211 techniques, sub-techniques explicitly omitted), MICRO-averaged over technique instances, OPEN-SOURCE models only, ONE corpus (The DFIR Report). (4) src-0021, 76.48% and 87.39% macro-F1 -- DOCUMENT-level, PARENT-level, MACRO-AVERAGED OVER DOCUMENTS, and a SCAFFOLD score rather than a bare-model score. FOUR AXES OF DIFFERENCE ARE IN PLAY AT ONCE -- unit of scoring (sentence vs document vs instance), label granularity (parent vs sub-technique), aggregation (micro vs macro-over-documents vs unknown), and system-vs-model -- and NO TWO OF THE FOUR AGREE ON ALL FOUR. THE SHARPEST INSTANCE, WHICH IS A METRIC-IDENTITY TRAP OF EXACTLY THE SHAPE ctr-0013 STANDS AS A WARNING ABOUT: src-0021's 'macro-F1' is a macro over DOCUMENTS, stated verbatim as 'F1bar = 1/|D| sum_{d in D} F1_d', whereas src-0002's Table 1 header 'Macro-F1' would on any conventional reading be a macro over TECHNIQUES. THESE ARE DIFFERENT STATISTICS SHARING A NAME, and the shared name is the only thing they share. SIMILARLY, src-0020 and src-0021 are BOTH parent-level, which is the single most tempting pairing in this base, and they are STILL NOT COMPARABLE: sentence-level micro over open-source bare models against document-level macro-over-documents over a frontier-backed scaffold. TWO PARENT-LEVEL SOURCES IS NOT TWO COMPARABLE MEASUREMENTS. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN HERE, stated as a question rather than a warning: is there any pair of published ATT&CK-extraction numbers in or reachable by this base that share unit, granularity, aggregation AND system-vs-model status, such that a genuine cross-source comparison could be made at all? If the answer is no, then this issue's honest resolution is a statement ABOUT THE MEASUREMENT LITERATURE -- that ATT&CK extraction reliability is reported in mutually unconvertible units and therefore has no established cross-study magnitude -- rather than a number. A T3 or T4 should treat that as a live candidate resolution in its own right and not as a failure to find one.

candidate_resolutions.summary: REWRITTEN IN PLACE AT CYCLE 31 BY A T3 EXECUTING ctr-0006's RESOLUTION PATH, STEPS (i) AND (ii). THE PRIOR TEXT IS NOT PRESERVED HERE BECAUSE graph.json IS NOT APPEND-ONLY-PROTECTED, BUT IT IS QUOTED IN FULL INSIDE ctr-0006 AND INSIDE THIS ISSUE'S CYCLE-29 scores.json RATIONALE, SO NOTHING IS LOST. WHAT WAS REMOVED AND WHY. (1) The quantified cross-task comparison, '0.6388 ... far below the ~71-72% accuracy the same models reach on knowledge-recall tasks'. src-0002's own metric paragraph forbids that subtraction: verbatim, 'We use accuracy to evaluate the CTI-MCQ and CTT-RCM tasks, as both tasks are equivalent to multi-class classification', against an F1 over a MULTI-LABEL space of 397 technique IDs. A multi-class accuracy with a non-trivial chance baseline and a multi-label F1 with a near-zero chance baseline are not differenceable quantities. The comparison was OURS and never the paper's: exact-string checks returned 'task difficulty' ABSENT and 'most challenging' ABSENT, and a third fetch asked for every sentence comparing performance BETWEEN tasks returned ABSENT. (2) The second sentence, which rested on src-0005 for the claim that the gap has not closed with newer models. Cycle 26 established that src-0005 REPORTS NO ATT&CK METRIC AT ALL, so it cannot support an ATT&CK claim in either direction. src-0005 IS ACCORDINGLY REMOVED FROM THIS CANDIDATE'S EVIDENCE LIST. WHAT THE SOURCE ACTUALLY SUPPORTS, STATED QUALITATIVELY. On CTIBench's CTI-ATE task -- extracting MITRE ATT&CK techniques from threat text and mapping them to technique IDs -- the best-performing model of the five evaluated (ChatGPT-4) reaches 0.6388, and no evaluated model exceeds that. The paper's own characterisation of the task is 'ChatGPT-4 significantly outperforms other models on the CTI-ATE task, underscoring the complexity of the task', which is a CROSS-MODEL observation and is the only textual anchor the paper offers. TWO METROLOGICAL LIMITS ARE NOW PART OF THE CLAIM RATHER THAN FOOTNOTES TO IT. (A) THE METRIC IDENTITY OF 0.6388 IS AMBIGUOUS BY THE PAPER'S OWN TEXT. Section 4.2 body text says 'We adopt the Micro-F1 score as the evaluation metric for the CTI-ATE task', while Table 1's column header reads 'CTI-ATE (Macro-F1)'. Micro-F1 and Macro-F1 are different quantities and diverge substantially over a 397-label multi-label space with a long tail. Both strings are PRESENT and verbatim in two independent fetches of arxiv.org/html/2406.07599v3. This is a defect IN THE SOURCE, not in this state, and it is unresolvable from the paper. (B) THE PAPER NEVER STATES HOW A PREDICTED TECHNIQUE COUNTS AS CORRECT -- exact technique ID, parent technique, sub-technique, or partial credit -- ABSENT in two fetches. So this leg reports a number whose metric is ambiguous and whose correctness rule is unstated, and cycle 31 could not repair either from the paper (see open_question 4). WHAT MUST NOT BE SAID, AND THIS IS THE STANDING PROHIBITION ctr-0006 EXISTS TO ENFORCE: that CTI-ATE is measurably harder than any other CTIBench task by a stated margin. Beyond the non-commensurability above, the ordering does not even hold naively in the direction the old text implied -- Table 1's CTI-TAA Correct column reads 52 for the same model, BELOW 63.88, so 'ATT&CK mapping is the worst task' is false on the paper's own printed numbers as well as unsupported by its text. FETCHING NOTE FOR ANY FUTURE CHECK: use arxiv.org/html/2406.07599v3 or the latest render. ARXIV v2 HAS NO CTI-ATE TASK AT ALL, so a v2 fetch returns spurious ABSENTs. PROVENANCE: every numeric cell involved is exact and the full ChatGPT-4 row has now been re-verified three separate times as 71.0 / 72.0 / 1.31 / 0.6388 / 52 / 86.

ADDED cycle 16 by T2, discharging carry-forward [2] which was cited in cycles 10 and 13 rationales but never attached to the graph. A third independent source now measures ATT&CK technique mapping and it lands FAR BELOW CTIBench's already-low ceiling. src-0007 (CyberThreat-Eval; Microsoft Research/Microsoft/HKUST, Mar 2026), on expert-annotated material drawn from a real company's daily CTI workflow, reports MITRE ATT&CK TTP identification precision/recall of 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o), 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini), 0.2387/0.1846 (fine-tuned GPT-4o) and 0.1771/0.1414 (fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini) -- against src-0002's CTI-ATE best-model F1 ceiling of 0.6388. THIS IS NOT A CONTRADICTION WITH src-0002 and no G3 entry was opened: different benchmark, different corpus, and a different metric decomposition (precision and recall separately, no F1), and real production material proving harder than a curated benchmark is the expected direction rather than a conflicting one. What src-0007 adds is twofold. (a) INDEPENDENCE: its authors are unaffiliated with CTIBench's and with PRISM/LANCE's, so the hardness of ATT&CK mapping is no longer resting on one team's benchmark design. (b) A WITHIN-TABLE CONTROL that cross-benchmark synthesis cannot supply: the identical models, on the identical corpus, through the identical harness, reach 0.8240-0.8846 precision on mechanical IoC extraction in the same table, so the ATT&CK deficit cannot be attributed to corpus difficulty or prompt harness quality. Provenance note: every figure quoted here was re-verified verbatim against the source by cycle 15's G2, exact to four decimal places, with no discrepancy. === CYCLE-31 ADDENDUM, APPENDED NOT SUBSTITUTED: CLAIM (b) IS NOW WITHDRAWN AND CLAIM (a) IS NARROWED. === Cycle 29's assessment held that this candidate's two distinctive contributions were both damaged, and cycle 31 read the missing scorer and can now say exactly how. (b) THE WITHIN-TABLE CONTROL DOES NOT SURVIVE AND MUST NOT BE CITED AGAIN. The argument was that because the identical models on the identical corpus through the identical harness reach 0.8240-0.8846 precision on mechanical IoC extraction in the same table, the ATT&CK deficit cannot be attributed to corpus difficulty or prompt harness quality. That inference silently assumed the two numbers were produced by comparable scoring. THEY ARE NOT, AND THE TWO RULES ARE NOW BOTH KNOWN FROM EXECUTING CODE IN THE SAME ARTEFACT. The IoC side (ctr-0004, cycle 27) is ONE-DIRECTIONAL SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT: any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set), so a prediction scores a true positive merely by being a substring of a ground-truth entry. The ATT&CK side (cycle 31, candidate 3) is EXACT TECHNIQUE-ID SET INTERSECTION with no partial credit of any kind. These are not two settings of one dial; they are different KINDS of matching, and the substring rule is the more permissive of the two on the axis that matters here. A comparison between a leniently scored number and a strictly scored number cannot license a conclusion about corpus or harness quality, which is precisely what claim (b) asserted. THE CONTROL IS WITHDRAWN. (a) INDEPENDENCE STANDS BUT DELIVERS LESS THAN CYCLE 16 CREDITED. src-0007's authors are genuinely unaffiliated with CTIBench's, so the finding that ATT&CK mapping scores low no longer rests on one team's benchmark design. But after ctr-0006 and cycle 31, the two legs are scored under rules that are (src-0007) known and strict, and (src-0002) unstated and metrically ambiguous. What the two independent sources jointly establish is therefore the DIRECTION of the finding -- ATT&CK technique mapping scores low on every measurement anyone has published -- and NOT any quantitative relationship between the two figures, which this candidate already disclaimed and which must stay disclaimed. WHAT IS UNCHANGED AND MUST NOT BE STRIPPED: all nine of src-0007's figures remain exact and remain the best-verified numbers in this base, and the fine-tuning result (0.2787/0.2270 for GPT-4o falling to 0.2387/0.1846 fine-tuned, and 0.1771/0.1414 for fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini) is untouched by anything above, since it is a WITHIN-COLUMN comparison scored by one rule against itself and is exactly the comparison the scorer supports best.

ADDED CYCLE 31. THE ATT&CK/TTP SCORING RULE BEHIND src-0007's TTP NUMBERS IS NOW KNOWN, READ OFF EXECUTING CODE, AND IT IS SUBSTANTIALLY STRICTER THAN ANY RULE PREVIOUSLY ASSUMED IN THIS BASE -- AND ITS OWN DOCUMENTATION DESCRIBES A DIFFERENT RULE FROM THE ONE IT RUNS. This is the fetch ctr-0006 step (iii), ctr-0001's remaining path and carry-forward [34] had all been asking for since cycle 24. The file is stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/eval/compute.py in the src-0017 artefact, retrieved WHOLE via raw.githubusercontent.com and read for which lines EXECUTE, per the ctr-0004 trap in which the IoC evaluator's documented rule turned out to live inside dead triple-quoted string literals. THE EXECUTING RULE, quoted verbatim from the live code. Ground truth per article: article_ttps_set = {ttp.split(' - ')[0].strip() for ttp in raw_ttps if ' - ' in ttp}. Predictions are a dict keyed by technique ID; each key is looked up in a mapping loaded from data/TTP_Mapping.csv, and the scoring set is validated_ttps_set = set(validated_ttps_final.keys()). Metrics: tp = len(article_ttps_set.intersection(validated_ttps_set)); fp = len(validated_ttps_set - article_ttps_set) + missing_in_mapping_count; fn = len(article_ttps_set - validated_ttps_set); then micro-averaged as overall_precision = total_tp / (total_tp + total_fp) and overall_recall = total_tp / (total_tp + total_fn). SO THE RULE IS EXACT STRING EQUALITY OF TECHNIQUE IDS, VIA SET INTERSECTION. There is no substring matching, no parent-technique credit, no sub-technique credit and no partial credit anywhere in the executing path. CONSEQUENCE THAT IS DIRECTLY ASSERTABLE, because TTP_Mapping.csv verifiably contains sub-technique IDs (T1548.001, T1548.002, T1548.003 and T1548.004 were quoted verbatim from it this cycle): if the ground truth says T1548 and a model predicts T1548.002, that prediction is admitted by the mapping check, fails the intersection, and is counted as a FALSE POSITIVE while T1548 is simultaneously counted as a FALSE NEGATIVE. One arguably-correct answer at the wrong granularity is penalised TWICE. SECOND FINDING, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS ctr-0004 BUT A DIFFERENT MECHANISM. The scorer's own docstring says, verbatim, 'If a TTP's description does not match the expected mapping, issue a warning and do NOT add this TTP to the final validated TTPs. (Such TTPs will be treated as false positives.)', and the directory README says the same in its own words -- 'Filtering: Only TTPs with matching descriptions are included' and, for a worked mismatch example, 'Result: Rejected (counted as false positive)'. THE CODE DOES THE OPPOSITE. On a description mismatch the live else-branch prints a warning and then executes corrected_details = ttp_mapping[ttp_id] followed by validated_ttps_final[ttp_id] = corrected_details -- it OVERWRITES the model's description with the canonical one and KEEPS the entry. There is no dead string literal here; the live code simply contradicts the docstring sitting above it in the same function. THE OPERATIVE CONSEQUENCE: the description check is INERT for scoring. A predicted technique ID counts on the sole condition that the ID appears in the mapping file, whatever the model wrote about it. So the scorer measures ID SELECTION ONLY, and any claim that it also measures whether the model correctly characterised the technique is false. THIRD FINDING, LENIENCY IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION, RECORDED SO THE BIAS IS NOT ASSUMED TO RUN ONE WAY: a per-article json5 parse failure executes 'continue' and the whole surrounding block is wrapped in a bare 'except Exception', so an article whose model output is malformed is DROPPED ENTIRELY -- contributing no false negatives for its ground truth and no false positives. Malformed output is not penalised; it is excluded from the micro-average. This is the one respect in which the rule is generous, and it cuts against the strictness above rather than reinforcing it. STATUS AND SCOPE, STATED PRECISELY BECAUSE THE TEMPTATION TO OVERREACH HERE IS LARGE. This candidate is supported as a claim about WHAT THE RELEASED SCORER DOES. It is NOT established that src-0007's Table 4 TTP figures were produced by this code: neither the paper nor the artefact says so, and the link is an inference from src-0017 being src-0007's release (see open_question 5). src-0017 is NOT INDEPENDENT of src-0007 -- same authors, same artefact -- so this pair can never serve as the two independent sources a strong claim requires; the claim is a direct reading of one artefact and needs no second source, but it also cannot borrow independence it does not have. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE ISSUE RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA: one of this issue's two comparands now has a stated, verified correctness rule and the other still has none. That is an improvement in the state of the evidence and simultaneously a demonstration that the two numbers were never comparable. === CYCLE-32 ADDENDUM, APPENDED NOT SUBSTITUTED. THIS CANDIDATE WAS RE-VERIFIED BY AN INDEPENDENT RE-FETCH AND IT PASSES; ONE FINDING IS ADDED THAT STRENGTHENS IT. === Cycle 32's G2 chose this candidate as its subject precisely because it was the newest, most load-bearing and least replicated conclusion in the graph -- a single fetch, made at cycle 31, on the strength of which ctr-0006 was CLOSED. stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/eval/compute.py was re-fetched whole from raw.githubusercontent.com and reproduced verbatim a second time, with ten exact-string checks run against the strings stored above. ALL TEN RETURNED PRESENT AND EXACT: the article_ttps_set comprehension, the validated_ttps_set assignment, the tp/fp/fn lines, the two overall_ ratio lines, the docstring sentence 'do NOT add this TTP to the final validated TTPs', corrected_details = ttp_mapping[ttp_id], validated_ttps_final[ttp_id] = corrected_details, json5 and except Exception. THE CRITICAL STRUCTURAL POINT WAS RE-CONFIRMED SPECIFICALLY AND SEPARATELY: the description-mismatch else-branch was reproduced with its indentation and the fetch was asked to state whether it is live executable code or sits inside a triple-quoted string, comment or docstring; the answer was that it is LIVE. So the docstring-versus-code contradiction is replicated, and this is not a second instance of the ctr-0004 dead-literal artefact. NOTHING IN THIS CANDIDATE IS RETRACTED OR NARROWED. THE ONE ADDITION, AND IT SHARPENS THE STRICTNESS FINDING RATHER THAN QUALIFYING IT. Cycle 32 read the head of data/TTP_Mapping.csv verbatim under an explicit instruction to make no claim about the whole file (it is 1,083,078 bytes and truncates -- see this issue's open_question 5 and cycle 31's own retraction). The header row is verbatim ',TechniqueID,name,longdescription,is sub-technique,sub-technique of,description,tactics', which on a 0-based naive comma split puts TechniqueID at field 1 and name at field 2, CONFIRMING that load_ttp_mapping's fields[1]/fields[2] do select the intended columns. BUT FIELD 5 IS 'sub-technique of', AND IT CARRIES THE PARENT ID. Verified verbatim on real data rows: T1548 appears with is sub-technique FALSE and an empty parent field, while T1548.001, T1548.002, T1548.003, T1548.004 and T1548.005 each appear with is sub-technique TRUE and 'sub-technique of' = T1548. load_ttp_mapping reads ONLY fields[1] and fields[2] and DISCARDS field 5. CONSEQUENCE: the parent-child relation needed to award parent-level credit for a sub-technique prediction is PRESENT IN THE SCORER'S OWN MAPPING FILE AND THROWN AWAY BY THE LOADER. The correct statement of this candidate's central finding is therefore not merely that the scorer implements no partial credit, but that it discards the data that would let it -- and that both legs of the double-penalty scenario asserted above are demonstrably reachable, since a parent ID and its sub-technique IDs are simultaneously admissible keys in the same mapping. TWO SMALLER POINTS, RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT MISTAKEN FOR DEFECTS LATER. (1) The naive parser's spurious keys, noted at cycle 31, are SCORING-INERT and here is the reason, which cycle 31 left unstated: continuation lines of quoted long descriptions do get parsed as candidate rows, but their fields[1] values are prose fragments that cannot equal a technique ID, and even in the improbable case that one did, the only thing it could corrupt is a mapped NAME -- and a name mismatch keeps the entry regardless, per this candidate's second finding. The pollution therefore cannot change any tp, fp or fn. (2) The header line itself satisfies the parser's conditions and enters the mapping as ttp_mapping['TechniqueID'] = 'name'; likewise inert. NO CONTRADICTION ENTRY WAS OPENED BY CYCLE 32 AND NONE WAS WARRANTED: this is a clean replication plus a strengthening addition, which is the outcome the G2 mechanism is supposed to be able to produce and had produced only twice in twelve source-checks before now.

issues.title: How reliable is LLM-assisted extraction of mechanical indicators of compromise (IPs, domains, URLs, hashes) from threat reports?
open_questions: STILL OPEN, BUT SHARPENED (cycle 9): no direct replication or critique of LANCE/PRISM exists -- cycle 6 searched for one and cycle 9 searched again over a wider net (see logs/cycle-009.md for exact queries), and 2603.09452 and 2605.06910 do not cite arXiv 2506.11325 at all. What now exists instead is an independent measurement of a DIFFERENT system on a DIFFERENT corpus (src-0007, vanilla LLM IoC extraction, precision 0.82-0.88) sitting ~10-15 points below LANCE's 97.6% F1. The live question is no longer 'has anyone replicated LANCE' (no) but 'is the gap between 97.6% and 0.82-0.88 explained by LANCE's regex pre-filter + human-validation loop, by corpus difficulty, or by the metric difference (F1 vs precision-only)?' Answering it needs a head-to-head: run LANCE on CyberThreat-Eval's IoC set, or run a vanilla LLM on PRISM. CYCLE-21 UPDATE -- ONE OF THE THREE BRANCHES IS NOW CLOSED, THE OTHER TWO ARE NOT. The METRIC branch is effectively eliminated (see the fourth candidate_resolution): cycle 18 computed that reconciling the two sources by the F1-vs-precision difference alone would require IoC recall of 0.09-0.15, and cycle 21 recovered src-0007's own Section 4.3 verdict that IoC extraction is 'relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary' -- a characterisation no author would write over a recall of 0.09-0.15. The SYSTEM branch is strengthened but still unmeasured, and the CORPUS branch is exactly where cycle 9 left it: nothing in the base compares PRISM's 50 public threat reports against src-0007's unnamed company's internal workflow for difficulty, and no cycle has attempted it. STILL NO HEAD-TO-HEAD EXISTS. Cycle 21 searched the artefact release rather than the literature, so the head-to-head search itself was not re-run this cycle -- but note carry-forward [6]: forward-citation sweeps have failed on two different arXiv ids and that is unavailable infrastructure, not an unsearched direction.

Does the result generalize beyond the 4 indicator types tested (IPs, domains, URLs, hashes) to e.g. registry keys, mutexes, YARA/Sigma rules? Cycle 9 note: src-0007 does NOT extend the coverage -- its ground truth is described as 'file hashes, IP addresses, or domain names'. Two independent benchmarks now both confine themselves to the same small family of network/file indicators, which suggests the field has not measured the harder indicator types at all rather than that they were measured and found comparable. CYCLE-21 UPDATE, AND THE COVERAGE IS NARROWER THAN RECORDED, NOT EQUAL. A verbatim pull of src-0007's annotation sentence gives 'concrete, structured artifacts--such as file hashes, IP addresses, or domain names'. URLs are NOT named. So src-0007 covers THREE indicator types against src-0003's four, and the two benchmarks' indicator families are not even coextensive with each other, let alone extended beyond the network/file family. The direction of the cycle-9 note is confirmed and its scope tightened: registry keys, mutexes and YARA/Sigma rules remain entirely unmeasured by any source in this base.

How much of LANCE's gain over IoC Searcher/AlienVault OTX/VirusTotal comes from the LLM component specifically vs. the regex pre-filtering and human-validation loop around it? Cycle 9 gives the first indirect evidence: src-0007's Table 4 is explicitly headed 'Vanilla LLMs' and a bare LLM there reaches only 0.82-0.85 precision on expert-annotated real-world data, which is consistent with (though it does not prove) the LLM component alone not being what delivers high-90s performance. Confounded by corpus and metric differences. CYCLE-21 UPDATE: THE METRIC CONFOUND IS NOW LIFTED FROM THIS QUESTION, THE CORPUS CONFOUND IS NOT, AND THE 'Vanilla LLMs' HEADING TURNS OUT TO BE WEAKER TEXTUAL EVIDENCE THAN NINE CYCLES OF NOTES HAVE ASSUMED. A whole-table pull confirms the caption verbatim as 'Performance Metrics for Vanilla LLMs by Task Category, Task, Metric, and Model' -- but two of the table's four columns are GPT-4o (FT) and GPT-4o-mini (FT), i.e. fine-tuned. 'Vanilla' therefore cannot mean 'not fine-tuned' in this paper's usage, and the only reading consistent with the columns is 'the LLM used directly, without an agentic or tool-scaffolded pipeline'. THE PAPER NEVER DEFINES THE TERM. That reading is an inference from column headers, not a quotation, and the whole system-confound argument rests on it. It should be labelled as an inference everywhere it is used. Note this cuts BOTH ways: it is still the best available textual evidence that src-0007 measures an unscaffolded system, and it is weaker evidence than 'explicitly headed' implies.

LARGELY ANSWERED AT CYCLE 21, RESIDUE STATED PRECISELY. Original (cycle 9): src-0007 reports precision only for IoC extraction, with no recall or F1 and no stated reason -- can recall/F1 be recovered from the released benchmark? ANSWERED, THREE PARTS. (a) NO, the number is not recoverable from the release: src-0017 shows stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/ holds data, eval, example and README.md, and the only prediction file anywhere is example/prediction/manual_ioc_predictions.json, a manual worked example. The paper's four model outputs are not published, so recall could only be obtained by re-running GPT-4o, o3-mini and the two fine-tunes. (b) BUT THE OMISSION IS NOW EXPLAINED AS A CHOICE, NOT A LIMIT: the released evaluator eval_ioc.py computes recall in the same function as precision and prints it on the very next line, with no code path that yields one without the other, and the sub-README treats recall as a first-class benchmark metric. src-0007 published the first line of that output and withheld the second. (c) The paper is NOT silent about recall either -- Section 4.3 reads 'In the TI drafting stage, the extraction of IoCs is relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary.' It still states no reason for the omission. RESIDUE, GENUINELY STILL OPEN: the numeric value; and whether the ground truth is EXHAUSTIVE per article, which src-0017's README never states -- recall against a non-exhaustive ground truth would not be comparable to recall against PRISM regardless. The README's displayed 'Overall Recall: 0.6667' is illustrative quick-start output against the manual example file and is NOT a measurement; no cycle may cite it. Unexplored: the HuggingFace mirror (huggingface.co/datasets/xse/CyberThreat-Eval) was not fetched and is where model outputs would live if they are released at all.

NEW (cycle 9): src-0008 shows LLM recovery of plaintext indicators from code is ~100% but collapses to ~0-1% under XOR/AES-256 concealment. Report-based extraction has never been evaluated under an adversarial threat model at all -- if report authors or adversaries defang/encode indicators (a routine practice in published reporting), does extraction accuracy degrade similarly? No source measures this. CYCLE-21: UNTOUCHED. This cycle did not reach this question and nothing found bears on it. It remains the issue's only wholly unaddressed question and is now the strongest candidate for a future T1's collection target, since no source in the base measures it and none is known to exist. CYCLE-35 RELABEL, ctr-0007 steps (ii) and (iii), APPENDED NOT SUBSTITUTED -- the text above stands but its two src-0008 figures are mis-labelled. The '~100%' and the '~0-1%' quoted above are FIGURE-DERIVED AND NOT TEXT-VERIFIED: src-0008's per-phase P0-P12 breakdown exists ONLY inside Figure 2 (caption 'LLM detection outcomes across all obfuscation phases (P0-P12)'), confirmed by two fetches instructed to write CANNOT READ rather than infer. What the body text supports verbatim is qualitative only: 'near-complete failure', 'encrypted IoCs become effectively opaque', 'once the code is encrypted, detection of IoCs remains essentially zero for all models'. A METRIC AMBIGUITY also travels with any src-0008 percentage: the paper defines detection rate twice, incompatibly -- body 'Detection rate, i.e., the proportion of samples in which the model correctly identifies the presence of an IoC' against Table 6's caption 'DR reflects the detection rate, i.e., ratio of YES an answers' -- so whether '~100%' means correctly-identified or answered-YES is UNDETERMINED BY THE PAPER. AND THE '~100%' IS NOT TRUE OF ALL FIVE MODELS: it holds for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok, while Cohere degrades progressively under purely syntactic obfuscation (1%/2%/5% misses at P1-P3, then 65% misses plus 35% Don't Know at P4). NONE OF THIS WEAKENS THE QUESTION ITSELF, which is about report-based extraction under an adversarial threat model and remains WHOLLY UNADDRESSED IN ITS TWENTY-SIXTH CYCLE.

NEW (cycle 21), and it undercuts the comparability of the 0.8240 precision figure itself rather than only the missing recall. src-0017's evaluator matches predicted IoCs to ground truth with a SUBSTRING rule in both directions -- its own comments read 'For prediction, if pred.lower() in ground truth or ground truth in pred' alongside 'Exact match'. A substring-permissive matcher inflates true positives relative to strict equality, so src-0007's precision is not a strict-match figure and may not be commensurable with src-0003's F1 even once a recall number exists. The full test() function body was not transcribed, so the exact conditions under which each rule fires are unknown. Resolving this needs the remainder of eval_ioc.py read, and ideally src-0003's own matching rule read alongside it -- a cheap, well-specified, high-value next step that requires no new search.

[6] NEW (cycle 35). THIS SUPERSEDES open_questions[5] ABOVE, WHICH IS LEFT IN PLACE PER THE APPEND-ONLY SPIRIT BUT IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. This discharges step (i) of ctr-0004, open since cycle 27. open_questions[5] says src-0017's evaluator matches 'with a SUBSTRING rule in both directions'. IT DOES NOT. The EXECUTING code in stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/eval/eval_ioc.py is ONE-DIRECTIONAL, verbatim: 'true_positives = sum(any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set) for pred in pred_list)', with 'false_positives = len(pred_list) - true_positives' and 'false_negatives = sum(not any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for pred in pred_list) for gt in gt_set)'. The two-directional variant and the exact-match variant are EACH ENCLOSED IN A TRIPLE-QUOTED STRING LITERAL and never execute; the comment lines cycle 21 quoted are the headers standing above those dead blocks. THE SOURCE STATES THE SAME RULE IN ITS OWN PROSE -- IoC sub-README, verbatim: 'A prediction is considered a True Positive (TP) if pred.lower() in gt.lower() for any ground truth IOC from the same source'. Code and documentation agree with each other and against what this issue said. THE CONSEQUENCE IS AN ASYMMETRIC BIAS, NOT A ONE-WAY ONE. The rule is LENIENT toward short or fragmentary predictions, since any prediction that is a substring of a longer ground-truth entry scores TP. It is STRICT against verbose predictions, since a prediction containing the ground-truth IoC plus surrounding text scores a FALSE POSITIVE -- and that is the characteristic failure mode of a free-form LLM extractor, i.e. exactly the case the dead two-directional block would have scored TP. A verbose-but-correct prediction is moreover penalised TWICE, as a false positive AND as a false negative, because the ground-truth entry it contains is simultaneously left unmatched by the false_negatives line above. So the limitation recorded at src-0017.md, that 'A substring-permissive matcher inflates true positives relative to strict equality', is HALF RIGHT and must never be repeated unqualified: relative to strict equality this matcher INFLATES on one axis and DEFLATES on the other, and THE NET SIGN IS UNKNOWN because it is the difference of two unmeasured quantities. PARTIAL MITIGATION, recorded so the deflation is not over-read: both sides pass through the same normalisation chain (transcribed verbatim in ctr-0004), which strips defanging -- hxxp to http, bracket removal -- and truncates at the first ' - ' separator, so the commonest verbose-prediction artefacts in CTI text are normalised away BEFORE matching. What survives the chain as verbose FP is free prose around the indicator, and a URL-with-path predicted against a bare-domain ground truth. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN: the net sign and magnitude of the bias. It cannot be recovered without the per-model prediction files, which are now confirmed ABSENT from both release mirrors -- see open_questions[7].

[7] NEW (cycle 35), AND IT CLOSES THE CHEAPEST REMAINING ROUTE ON ctr-0001 RATHER THAN OPENING ONE. huggingface.co/datasets/xse/CyberThreat-Eval was named as the cheapest unexplored step in ctr-0001's cycle-21 update and in open_questions[3], and had never been fetched by any cycle. IT WAS FETCHED THIS CYCLE, THREE URL FORMS, AND THE PER-MODEL IoC PREDICTIONS ARE NOT THERE. The HuggingFace tree API (huggingface.co/api/datasets/xse/CyberThreat-Eval/tree/main?recursive=true) returns a COMPLETE 52-file listing WITH BYTE SIZES, so this is an authoritative absence and not a truncated render. The only prediction artefact anywhere under the IoC task is stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/example/prediction/manual_ioc_predictions.json at 1,298 bytes -- the manual worked example already known from the GitHub mirror, far too small to be four models' output over 1,310 IoCs. The only other model-named file in the whole repository is stage3_ti_drafting/score_evaluation/example/test_output/gpt-4o.json at 8,571 bytes, which belongs to the threat-actor/root-cause SCORING task and is likewise an example. THE MIRROR IS THE SAME REPOSITORY, NOT A SUPERSET: stage3_ti_drafting/ttp/data/TTP_Mapping.csv is 1,083,078 bytes, byte-for-byte the size cycle 31 recorded from GitHub. CONSEQUENCE: src-0007's unreported IoC recall is NOT obtainable from any released artefact, and the only remaining route is re-running GPT-4o, o3-mini and the two fine-tunes, which is outside this loop's means. ctr-0001's METRIC confound therefore stays 'eliminated by argument' and can no longer be 'settled by number' from the release. SECOND QUESTION ASKED AND ANSWERED IN THE NEGATIVE: whether the ground truth is stated to be EXHAUSTIVE per article. ABSENT, confirmed at two URL forms (the rendered dataset card and the raw README at /resolve/main/README.md), consistent with the IoC sub-README read whole at cycle 27. So even if a recall number existed it would be recall against a ground truth of unstated completeness, which is not comparable with PRISM's regardless -- this residue of open_questions[3] is now CONFIRMED OPEN AT SOURCE rather than merely suspected, and it is a permanent limit on the comparison, not a fetch away from closing.

candidate_resolutions.summary: For narrow, mechanical IoC extraction (as opposed to open-ended CTI reasoning), a hybrid regex+LLM+human-validation pipeline (LANCE) reached 97.6% F1 against the manually-validated PRISM benchmark, substantially outperforming legacy tools (IoC Searcher+whitelist 76%, AlienVault OTX 72%, VirusTotal@threshold=1 86%) and also improving downstream analyst speed (43% less annotation time) and downstream model training data quality (+6% F1). This is a single-study result from the benchmark's own authors, not yet independently replicated.

ADDED cycle 9. A second, fully independent measurement of LLM IoC extraction from real-world CTI material now exists: CyberThreat-Eval (src-0007; Microsoft Research/Microsoft/HKUST, Mar 2026), an expert-annotated benchmark built from a production CTI workflow covering 1310 IoCs, reports vanilla-LLM extraction precision of 0.8240 (GPT-4o), 0.8503 (o3-mini), 0.8846 (fine-tuned GPT-4o) and 0.6944 (fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini). Read narrowly, this establishes that a bare LLM prompted to extract indicators from real analyst-workflow material errs on roughly 1 in 6 of the indicators it emits -- materially short of the near-solved impression left by src-0003's 97.6% F1, and short of even the 86% VirusTotal@threshold=1 baseline src-0003 reports. It does NOT refute src-0003, because it measures a different system (no regex pre-filter, no human validation loop), on a different corpus, with a different metric (precision only; no recall or F1 given). See contradiction ctr-0001, opened this cycle rather than resolved either way.

ADDED cycle 9, deliberately weak status. Candidate synthesis: the reliability of mechanical IoC extraction is set mainly by the scaffolding around the model (regex pre-filtering, whitelisting, human validation) rather than by the LLM itself, which is why src-0003's scaffolded pipeline reports 97.6% F1 while src-0007's 'Vanilla LLMs' reach 0.82-0.88 precision and src-0008 finds an unscaffolded LLM recovers plaintext indicators ~100% of the time but is defeated entirely by encryption it has no tooling for. [SENTENCE CORRECTED AT CYCLE 35, ctr-0007 step (i) -- THE PRECEDING CLAUSE ABOUT src-0008 IS FALSE AND IS RETAINED ONLY SO THE CORRECTION IS AUDITABLE; DO NOT CITE IT. src-0008 evaluates FIVE models, not one and not four, and ENCRYPTION IS NOT THE BOUNDARY FOR ALL OF THEM. Body text verbatim: 'ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok achieve 100% across all four phases without reporting uncertainties' -- and immediately after it -- 'Cohere, however, shows progressive degradation: 1% missed detections in P1, 2% in P2, 5% in P3, and in P4, 65% misses plus 35% explicit Don't Know responses'. Phases P1-P4 contain NO CRYPTOGRAPHY: Table 3 defines them verbatim as '1. Base64 encoding', '2. Identifier obfuscation', '3. Dead code injection', '4. Structural obfuscation'. So one of five models loses roughly two thirds of its detections under PURELY SYNTACTIC transformation that leaves the indicator in plain text. THE CORRECT STATEMENT IS: four of src-0008's five models recover plaintext indicators at 100% through four levels of syntactic obfuscation and then fail near-completely once the indicator is encrypted, while the fifth degrades progressively under syntactic obfuscation alone. TWO CITATION CONSTRAINTS TRAVEL WITH ANY src-0008 PERCENTAGE USED HERE, per ctr-0007 steps (ii) and (iii). (a) FIGURE-DERIVED: the per-phase P0-P12 breakdown exists ONLY inside Figure 2, confirmed by two fetches instructed to write CANNOT READ rather than infer, so the '~0-1%' and '~95%+ misses' figures are FIGURE-DERIVED AND NOT TEXT-VERIFIED; what the body text supports verbatim is qualitative only ('near-complete failure', 'encrypted IoCs become effectively opaque'). (b) METRIC AMBIGUITY: the paper defines its own detection rate twice, incompatibly -- body 'Detection rate, i.e., the proportion of samples in which the model correctly identifies the presence of an IoC' against Table 6's caption 'DR reflects the detection rate, i.e., ratio of YES an answers' -- and a ratio of YES answers does not require correctness, so whether '100% detection' means correctly-identified or answered-YES is UNDETERMINED BY THE PAPER.] This is a plausible reading of three sources that were never designed to be compared, and no source tests it directly -- it is recorded as proposed so a later cycle can attack it, NOT as a finding. CYCLE-21 ATTACKED IT AND IT SURVIVES, BUT IT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT AT 'proposed'. What changed: the competing explanation for the same evidence -- that the src-0003/src-0007 gap is a metric artefact -- is now effectively eliminated (see the fourth candidate_resolution), which removes the main rival reading and leaves scaffolding as the live explanation. What did NOT change: no source tests this claim directly, no head-to-head exists, the corpus confound is completely unaddressed, and the 'Vanilla LLMs' heading that anchors the claim turns out to be an inference rather than a definition (see open_questions). Eliminating one rival explanation is not the same as demonstrating a causal claim about scaffolding, and promoting on that basis would be exactly the over-reach this candidate was created to resist. It stays 'proposed'. CYCLE-35 DECISION ON ctr-0007's OPEN QUESTION, WHICH CYCLE 29 EXPLICITLY DECLINED TO ANSWER. The question put was: does large model-side variance under PURELY SYNTACTIC noise SUPPORT the scaffolding hypothesis (regex pre-filtering and whitelisting are indifferent to dead-code injection and control-flow flattening, so scaffolding is what buys robustness) or UNDERCUT it (the variance is model-side, i.e. the model is exactly what varies)? I DECIDE THAT IT CUTS BOTH WAYS, AND THE CANDIDATE STAYS 'proposed' -- but that is a decision with content, not a refusal to decide, because the two readings turn out to be about DIFFERENT PROPOSITIONS and both can be true at once. (1) THE UNDERCUTTING READING IS THE STRONGER OF THE TWO ON THIS EVIDENCE. Five models, one corpus, one task, NO scaffolding on any arm, and a spread running from 100% to roughly 35% at P4. If the model were not what sets reliability, that spread could not exist. Model identity is therefore a large variance component under unscaffolded conditions, which is a direct qualification of a hypothesis whose whole content is that reliability is set 'mainly by the scaffolding around the model rather than by the LLM itself'. (2) THE SUPPORTING READING IS REAL BUT IS A COUNTERFACTUAL, NOT A MEASUREMENT. It is true that a regex extractor would be indifferent to dead-code injection and structural obfuscation, since those transformations leave the indicator in plain text; so scaffolding WOULD plausibly have erased Cohere's degradation. But src-0008 RUNS NO SCAFFOLDED ARM, so this is an inference about an experiment nobody performed, and it must not be entered as evidence. (3) THE DECISIVE POINT, AND IT IS WHY NEITHER READING PROMOTES OR DEMOTES THE CANDIDATE: src-0008 CANNOT ADJUDICATE THIS HYPOTHESIS AT ALL. Its task is recovering a planted indicator from JavaScript SOURCE CODE under adversarial transformation; this candidate is about extracting indicators from NARRATIVE THREAT REPORTS. The scope limit was already recorded at src-0008 key_claims[2] and this cycle enforces it. src-0008's role in this candidate is accordingly DEMOTED from evidence-for-the-boundary to ILLUSTRATION ONLY, and a weak one, further weakened by the metric ambiguity and the image-locked per-phase figures noted above. src-0008 IS RETAINED in the evidence list because removing it would erase the trail, NOT because it supports the claim. NET EFFECT ON THE CANDIDATE'S STANDING: the hypothesis now rests on the src-0003-versus-src-0007 contrast alone, i.e. on two sources that were never designed to be compared, with the corpus confound untouched and the 'Vanilla LLMs' anchor known to be an inference. That is WEAKER than the position cycle 21 left it in, since cycle 21's ground for keeping it alive was that eliminating the metric rival left scaffolding as the live explanation, and this cycle adds a second live explanation -- MODEL IDENTITY -- that no cycle had put on the board. A future cycle should treat 'model choice sets the floor, scaffolding sets the ceiling' as the compatible third reading and test it, rather than treating scaffolding and model as rivals.

ADDED cycle 21, and this is the cycle's substantive result. THE METRIC CONFOUND CANNOT ACCOUNT FOR THE src-0003 / src-0007 GAP, so ctr-0001 does not dissolve into an artefact of comparing an F1 with a precision. Two independent lines converge. (1) ARITHMETIC (cycle 18): for src-0007's unreported IoC recall to drag an F1 down far enough to reconcile 97.6% with a precision of 0.82-0.88, recall would have to fall in the range 0.09-0.15. (2) THE AUTHORS' OWN VERDICT (cycle 21, newly recovered from Section 4.3 of arXiv 2603.09452v1, verbatim): 'In the TI drafting stage, the extraction of IoCs is relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary.' A team describing their own system's IoC extraction as 'relatively robust' with recall merely needing 'improvements' is not describing recall of 0.09-0.15 -- particularly when the same paper flatly calls the TTP task, at recall 0.1414-0.2270, 'a substantial challenge'. The paper's own contrast between the two tasks puts IoC recall well above the reconciling range. SUPPORTING CONTEXT from src-0017: the omission is not a measurement limitation but a reporting decision -- the released evaluator computes recall in the same function as precision and prints it on the next line. INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT, STATED PLAINLY: both textual legs come from the same author team, and src-0017 is the same team's artefact, so this rests on ONE independent measurement plus arithmetic over src-0003's published figure, not on two independent measurements. It is an ELIMINATIVE claim -- it rules a confound out; it does not establish what the gap IS. The SYSTEM and CORPUS confounds both remain live, and ctr-0001 accordingly stays OPEN. [CYCLE-35 ADDENDUM, EXECUTING ctr-0004 STEP (ii). THE HEADLINE ELIMINATIVE CLAIM SURVIVES AND IS NOW ON STRICTLY BETTER GROUND, BUT LEG (1) AS STATED ABOVE IS MIS-SCOPED AND IS RESTATED HERE; see ctr-0010, opened this cycle. NOTHING ABOVE IS DELETED.] (A) WHAT THE 0.09-0.15 FIGURE ACTUALLY IS. Leg (1) above says the range is what 'reconciling 97.6% with a precision of 0.82-0.88' would require. IT IS NOT. logs/cycle-018.md prints the derivation as a four-row table headed 'Solving 2PR/(P+R) for the unreported IoC recall at which each model's IoC F1 falls to its own derived TTP F1', with columns model / IoC precision / derived TTP F1 / crossover recall / actual TTP recall: GPT-4o 0.8240 / 0.2502 / 0.1475 / 0.2270; o3-mini 0.8503 / 0.2337 / 0.1354 / 0.1759; GPT-4o (FT) 0.8846 / 0.2082 / 0.1180 / 0.1846; GPT-4o-mini (FT) 0.6944 / 0.1572 / 0.0887 / 0.1414. So 0.09-0.15 is a WITHIN-src-0007 quantity -- the IoC recall at which src-0007's IoC task would score no better than src-0007's OWN TTP task -- and src-0003's 97.6% ENTERS IT NOWHERE. Cycle 18's own carry-forward [7] restated it as a src-0003 reconciliation and every downstream use in this graph and in scores.json inherited that restatement. The ARGUMENT cycle 18 built on it is untouched and remains good: every crossover sits BELOW that model's own TTP recall by a factor of 1.3-1.6, so IoC recall would have to be worse than TTP recall on a task the same authors call 'relatively robust' while calling TTP 'a substantial challenge'. (B) DOES THE ONE-DIRECTIONAL ASYMMETRY CHANGE THAT ARITHMETIC? NO, AND THE INSENSITIVITY IS DERIVED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The matcher enters only through P. Solving 2PR/(P+R) = F for R gives R = FP/(2P-F), whence dR/dP = -F squared / (2P-F) squared. For GPT-4o (F = 0.2502, P = 0.8240) that is -0.0626/1.9538 = -0.0320. A correction to P of a full 0.13 in either direction therefore moves the crossover recall by about 0.004. Worked at the extreme: if the matcher were deflating GPT-4o's precision all the way from 0.8240 to 0.9531, the crossover moves from 0.1475 to 0.1440. THE 0.09-0.15 RANGE IS ROBUST TO THE MATCHER ASYMMETRY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. (One second-order effect is noted and is neutral: the same one-directional rule deflates measured RECALL as well as measured precision, since a verbose-but-correct prediction is scored FP and FN together -- but the crossover threshold, the authors' Section 4.3 characterisation and eval_ioc.py's printed output are all in the SAME matcher-measured units, so the comparison is internally consistent.) (C) THE src-0003 RECONCILIATION, DONE PROPERLY FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND IT NEEDS NO RECALL VALUE AT ALL. F1 = 2PR/(P+R) is increasing in R, so for any system F1 <= 2P/(P+1). Setting 2P/(P+1) >= 0.976 gives 1.024P >= 0.976, i.e. P >= 0.9531. LANCE's published 97.6% F1 therefore ENTAILS a precision of at least 0.9531. That is a PRECISION, and src-0007's 0.8240-0.8846 are PRECISIONS, so the two sources can be compared like with like and the F1-versus-precision mismatch that defines ctr-0001's METRIC confound simply does not arise. THE METRIC CONFOUND IS ELIMINATED DEDUCTIVELY, not by a plausibility argument, and no value of src-0007's missing recall can revive it. MARGIN, AS REQUIRED: 0.9531 - 0.8846 = 0.069 against src-0007's BEST model, and 0.9531 - 0.8240 = 0.129 against vanilla GPT-4o. (D) WHAT THE ASYMMETRY DOES INSTEAD -- IT CREATES A FOURTH CONFOUND RATHER THAN REVIVING THE SECOND. Call it MATCHER. For it to close the 0.069 gap, src-0007's one-directional rule would have to be NET-DEFLATING its precision by 6.9 points, i.e. at least 6.9% of the fine-tuned model's emitted IoCs would have to be verbose-but-correct predictions scored FP. That is not absurd -- it is the characteristic free-form-LLM failure mode -- but three things stop it being asserted: the rule is simultaneously LENIENT toward fragmentary predictions so the net is a difference of two unmeasured quantities of unknown sign; the shared normalisation chain already strips defanging and truncates at ' - ', closing the commonest deflation channel before matching; and src-0003 NEVER STATES ITS OWN MATCHING RULE (src-0003.md line 141), so LANCE's entailed 0.9531 may itself be leniently scored and the correction could run either way on BOTH sides. (E) VERDICT ON THIS CANDIDATE'S STATUS. It stays 'supported' and it is NOT over-claimed in its headline: the METRIC confound cannot account for the gap, and after (C) that is a stronger result than when it was written. What is defective is its stated leg (1), which attributes to the 0.09-0.15 range a scope that range does not have; ctr-0010 records that rather than the edit being made silently. ctr-0001 STAYS OPEN, now against THREE live confounds -- SYSTEM (unmeasured), CORPUS (untouched) and MATCHER (new, and not settleable from any released artefact, per open_questions[7]).

issues.title: Beyond raw accuracy, are LLM-generated CTI outputs consistent across repeated queries and well-calibrated in stated confidence?
open_questions: ANSWERED AT CYCLE 25 IN THE NEGATIVE, AND RESTATED AS WHAT REMAINS. src-0001's Table 6 was pulled whole for the first time at cycle 25 (caption verbatim: 'ECE and BS with gpt4o for information generation and extraction'). It is gpt4o-ONLY and complete at NINE rows -- extraction campaign/APT/CVE/attack vector, generation goals/labels/country/CVE/attack vector -- across all three paradigms; the base had stored only five of those rows. The paper reports NO ECE or Brier figure for gemini-1.5-pro-latest or mistral-large-2 ANYWHERE, so the gpt4o-specificity question cannot be settled from this source at all. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: whether the fine-tuning-can-worsen-calibration pattern is gpt4o-specific now requires a NEW measurement of proper-scoring calibration on a CTI task for a non-gpt4o model, and no such measurement exists in this base or was found by cycle 25's searches.

STILL FULLY OPEN, AND CYCLE 25 WIDENED RATHER THAN NARROWED IT. None of src-0001's 3 tested models (gpt4o, gemini-1.5-pro-latest, mistral-large-2) overlaps src-0002's (GPT-4-turbo, GPT-3.5-turbo, Gemini-1.5, LLAMA3-70B/8B) or src-0005's lists -- would the consistency/calibration findings replicate on the specific models shown to struggle with ATT&CK mapping and attribution in those benchmarks? src-0018, added this cycle, does NOT answer it either: its five models (GPT-4.1, GPT-5, GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Opus 4.5) overlap NO list in this base. So the base now has CTI-task consistency evidence on two disjoint model sets a generation apart, and zero per-model replication on any single model.

Does the multi-dimensional reliability framing (accuracy + consistency + calibration) proposed in src-0001 apply equally across the other CTI sub-tasks measured in src-0002/src-0005 (MCQ, RCM, ATE, TAA, malware analysis), or was it only measured in src-0001's own information-extraction/-generation evaluation setting?

NARROWED AT CYCLE 25, STILL OPEN. Fine-tuning and few-shot were both shown to sometimes worsen accuracy and calibration (gpt4o APT-extraction P/R 0.87->0.68 after fine-tuning; CVE-generation ECE 0.15->0.91, both re-verified exact this cycle) -- is this degradation specific to small fine-tuning dataset size / overfitting, or a general risk for CTI fine-tuning regardless of data volume? WHAT CYCLE 25 ESTABLISHED: the paper NOWHERE attributes the degradation to dataset size or overfitting (checked explicitly), so it offers no answer, and the only sentence bearing on the fine-tuning set size came back ELIDED from the fetch ('We randomly select 70% of the dataset...70% to the few-shot examples section and fine-tuning') and is therefore NOT verbatim-captured. Two concrete next steps: re-pull that split sentence verbatim, and note that the fine-tuning pool is bounded above by 350 reports either way, which makes small-data overfitting a live but unconfirmed explanation. === CYCLE 39: THE NAMED UNDONE STEP IS DISCHARGED, THE BOUND CYCLE 25 RECORDED WAS WRONG, AND THE UNDERLYING QUESTION NARROWS BUT STAYS OPEN. The split passage is now captured WHOLE AND UNELIDED, identical from two URL forms (arxiv.org/html/2503.23175v1 and the unversioned render, which is v4), verbatim: 'Dataset division. We randomly select 70% of the dataset, thus mimicking the splitting which is typical of ML and DL model validations. In ML and DL, the splitting would have been in training, validation, and testing respectively in portions of 70%, 20%, and 10%. Since we do not train from scratch our model we assign 70% to the few-shot examples section and fine-tuning and 30% for the testing. We employ this division to avoid overfitting both for fine-tuning and for few-shot learning, if the few-shot examples are gathered directly from the dataset on which testing is conducted.' CORRECTION TO CYCLE 25: the fine-tuning pool is NOT bounded above by 350 reports. It is bounded by 70% of 350 = 245 reports (AGENT-DERIVED; the paper prints only '# of reports: 350' and the percentages), and that 245 is SHARED with the few-shot example pool, so fine-tuning alone used at most 245 and possibly far fewer. Test set is 30% = 105 reports (AGENT-DERIVED). THE EXACT NUMBER OF REPORTS USED FOR FINE-TUNING IS ABSENT, confirmed against two URL forms. SO IS THE ENTIRE FINE-TUNING SETUP: no hyperparameters, no epoch count, no learning rate, no endpoint, no fine-tuning-set size appear anywhere in the paper, confirmed ABSENT by two fetches on two URL forms, each permitted to answer ABSENT. This is a real reporting limitation of src-0001 and had never been recorded. CYCLE 25's 'the paper NOWHERE attributes the degradation to dataset size or overfitting' is CONFIRMED, but it must be scoped more precisely than cycle 25 scoped it: the word 'overfitting' DOES occur in the paper, twice, and both occurrences are about the SPLIT DESIGN rather than about the observed degradation -- the sentence above, and 'To control for prompt overfitting ... we evaluate the LLMs on the part of the dataset from which we do not gather any few-shot examples'. The paper invokes overfitting only as something its design controls FOR, never as an explanation of what it measured, and that control is asserted rather than measured. WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS OPEN: whether the post-fine-tuning calibration collapse is a small-data or overfitting artefact CANNOT BE ANSWERED FROM src-0001 AT ALL, because the paper reports neither the fine-tuning set size nor any fine-tuning configuration. A 245-report ceiling is small in absolute terms for fine-tuning, so a small-data explanation is AVAILABLE but remains UNTESTED AND UNASSERTED. Answering this now requires a source that fine-tunes on CTI at more than one data volume and reports calibration at each; no such source is in this base.

NEW AT CYCLE 25, AND THE CHEAPEST HIGH-VALUE ITEM ON THIS LIST. Every quantitative artefact in src-0018 is an IMAGE and none of its numbers is recoverable by this agent's fetch tooling: the table 'LLM decision consistency' (five models x {is_compromised, attack_stage} x {% of IOCs with P_o < 1, D-bar_o}), the chart 'Abstention error rates' (FDR/FNR per model), and the charts 'Selective IOC extraction performance' and 'Value assignment performance'. Two fetches instructed to answer 'IMAGE - CANNOT READ' rather than infer both did so. Until those cells are read, src-0018 supports DIRECTION only and supplies no magnitude to compare against src-0001's CI widths of 0.02 (extraction) and 0.06 (generation). Is there another route -- a companion paper, a conference talk, a PDF version, or alt-text? Cycle 25 searched for an arXiv companion by Milenkoski and Cirstea and found none.

NEW AT CYCLE 25. Does ANY source measure proper-scoring confidence calibration (ECE, Brier, reliability diagrams) on a CTI task other than src-0001? Cycle 25 ran three targeted searches and found none. Two leads were positively KILLED rather than left dangling: CTIArena (arXiv 2510.11974, Cheng/Liu/Li/Song/Gao, Virginia Tech and UC Berkeley; 9 CTI tasks, 10 models) was fetched and measures NEITHER repeat-query consistency NOR calibration/abstention, so it is not a candidate for this issue and should not be re-proposed for it; and no arXiv companion exists for src-0018. The calibration half of this issue therefore remains SINGLE-SOURCE on CTI (src-0001 alone) even though the consistency half is now two-source. === CYCLE 39 SPENT NO SEARCH BUDGET ON THIS AND IT IS UNCHANGED. Cycle 39's four fetches all went to the ctr-0003 resolution and the G2, which was the right call given ctr-0003 had been open fourteen cycles, but it means this question has now gone fourteen cycles without a new search. IT REMAINS THE HIGHEST-VALUE ITEM ON THIS LIST for the reason cycle 36 gave and cycles 37 and 39 endorse: a second CTI-task ECE/Brier source is the single measurement that would let a T4 move this issue off 2, because the level-3 bar requires the PRIMARY candidate -- the one answering BOTH conjuncts of the title -- to have two independent sources, and that candidate rests on src-0001 alone. Do NOT re-propose CTIArena (arXiv 2510.11974); cycle 25 killed it at source. CYCLE 39 ADDS A REASON THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT DID BEFORE: the calibration leg is not merely single-source, it is single-source, single-model (gpt4o only) and now, per the new open_question below, INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT BETWEEN ITS TWO METRICS. A second source would be doing more work than simple corroboration.

NEW AT CYCLE 39, RAISED BY THE ctr-0003 RESOLUTION AND NOT ANSWERABLE FROM THIS BASE. src-0001's Table 6 reports ECE and Brier Score side by side and the paper defines them identically, verbatim: 'The ECE and BS, are two measures of calibration that quantify the deviation from perfect calibration.' BUT THE TWO METRICS ORDER THE TWO TASK FAMILIES DIFFERENTLY. On family means derived by cycle 39 from the printed cells (all AGENT-DERIVED, not printed), generation is worse than extraction on ECE at all three paradigms (0.278 vs 0.205 zero-shot, 0.320 vs 0.2425 few-shot, 0.538 vs 0.295 fine-tuned) but on Brier the gap is nil at zero-shot (0.304 vs 0.2975) and REVERSED at few-shot (0.294 vs 0.3225). A single row disagrees outright: extraction attack vector is the best-calibrated extraction cell on zero-shot ECE (0.13) and the worst on zero-shot BS (0.46). THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHICH METRIC SHOULD GOVERN A CALIBRATION CLAIM ON CTI, AND WHY. The paper does not distinguish them, offers no reliability diagram, and never comments on the divergence; this base has no source that discusses ECE-versus-Brier behaviour at all. An answer needs either a methodological source on proper scoring rules versus binned calibration error, or a CTI source reporting both metrics with a stated preference. UNTIL THEN, NO CYCLE MAY STATE AN EXTRACTION-VERSUS-GENERATION CALIBRATION GRADIENT WITHOUT NAMING THE METRIC IT HOLDS ON, and the only paradigm at which it holds on BOTH metrics is fine-tuning. This bears directly on extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis and task-dependent-reliability-framing, both of which use src-0001's extraction-versus-generation split as a calibration data point; a T3 targeting either must read this before citing it. NOTE THAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH THE CONSISTENCY HALF, where the CI widths of 0.02 against 0.06 are a single measurement with no competing metric.

NEW AT CYCLE 39, PROVENANCE, AND CHEAP FOR THE NEXT CYCLE THAT TOUCHES src-0001. Cycle 25 upgraded src-0001 from 'unreviewed preprint' to 'PEER-REVIEWED AND PUBLISHED at ARES 2025' on the strength of a citation block on the arXiv /html render giving 'In International Conference on Availability, Reliability and Security (pp. 343-364). Cham: Springer Nature Switzerland' and a conference DOI of 10.1007/978-3-032-00627-1_17. Cycle 39 fetched arxiv.org/abs/2503.23175 and found that arXiv's OWN METADATA FIELDS DO NOT CARRY IT: the Comments line is ABSENT, the Journal reference line is ABSENT, and the only DOI listed is the arXiv DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2503.23175. Contrast src-0007, whose /abs page does carry both 'Comments: Accepted at TMLR' and a Journal reference. THIS IS NOT A CONTRADICTION -- an /html citation block can legitimately carry a venue the /abs metadata omits, and the four listed versions all predate nothing that would explain it -- BUT IT MEANS THE PEER-REVIEW STATUS OF THIS BASE'S MOST LOAD-BEARING SOURCE RESTS ON A SINGLE UNCORROBORATED ARTEFACT. One fetch of https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-00627-1_17 would settle it. Cycle 39 did not spend that fetch and flags it as the cheapest outstanding provenance item in the base.

candidate_resolutions.summary: Reliability for CTI cannot be reduced to accuracy alone: on a 350-real-report evaluation, tested LLMs were both inconsistent across repeated/paraphrased queries and overconfident relative to their actual correctness, and this did not resolve with few-shot learning or fine-tuning (only partial improvement across all three paradigms tested). Exact per-model numeric scores are not yet captured in our knowledge base and are needed before this can be scored as strongly (vs. qualitatively) supported. === SCOPING NOTE ADDED AT CYCLE 39 WHILE RESOLVING ctr-0003. ctr-0003 named 'candidate_resolutions 1 and 2' as carriers of the disputed extraction-versus-generation calibration gradient. On inspection THIS candidate carries no gradient claim at all: its only calibration word is 'overconfident', which is the paper's own abstract term ('We show how LLMs cannot guarantee sufficient performance on real-size reports while also being inconsistent and overconfident.', re-verified verbatim from arxiv.org/abs/2503.23175 at cycle 39) and is not a between-task comparison. THIS CANDIDATE IS THEREFORE UNCHANGED BY ctr-0003 and no rewrite was needed here; the retirement was applied to the next candidate only, which is the one that actually states the gradient. Recorded so that no later cycle reads ctr-0003 and concludes this candidate was overlooked.

Full-text retrieval (cycle 3) confirms and sharpens the above with concrete numbers. The 3 tested models were gpt4o, gemini-1.5-pro-latest, and mistral-large-2. Consistency (10-re-prompt bootstrapped confidence intervals) was tight for mechanical information-extraction (max CI width 0.02) but notably wider for open-ended information-generation (max CI width 0.06). Calibration (ECE/Brier, gpt4o) was substantially worse for generation than extraction sub-tasks, and critically, fine-tuning and few-shot prompting often WORSENED both accuracy and calibration rather than uniformly 'partially improving' them -- e.g. gpt4o APT-extraction precision/recall fell from 0.87 (zero-shot) to 0.68 (fine-tuned), and CVE-generation ECE rose from 0.15 to 0.91 after fine-tuning. This refines the cycle-2 resolution: the unreliability is not just persistent across paradigms -- more training examples or fine-tuning can actively degrade both accuracy and calibration on some CTI sub-tasks. === REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 39 TO RESOLVE ctr-0003. THE 'SUBSTANTIALLY WORSE FOR GENERATION THAN EXTRACTION' CALIBRATION FRAMING IN THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS HEREBY RETIRED AS UNSUPPORTED. Everything else in this candidate stands and every number in it is re-verified exact; only the calibration GRADIENT is withdrawn. WHY IT IS RETIRED: it does not hold row-wise at zero-shot -- generation goals 0.13, CVE 0.15 and country 0.19 all beat extraction campaign 0.25 and CVE 0.28 -- and its own worked example, CVE generation at 0.15, is better calibrated than its extraction counterpart at 0.28. THE REPLACEMENT IS NARROWER THAN THE RESTATEMENT ctr-0003 PROPOSED, BECAUSE CYCLE 39 FOUND THE GRADIENT IS METRIC-DEPENDENT. Per methodological rule (xii) cycle 39 re-derived every family mean from Table 6's printed cells itself rather than inheriting ctr-0003's figures. ctr-0003's FOUR ECE MEANS REPRODUCE EXACTLY: zero-shot extraction 0.205 (0.25+0.16+0.28+0.13 = 0.82, /4) against generation 0.278 (0.13+0.45+0.19+0.15+0.47 = 1.39, /5); fine-tuned extraction 0.295 (1.18/4) against generation 0.538 (2.69/5). The two few-shot ECE means, never derived by any prior cycle: extraction 0.2425 (0.97/4), generation 0.320 (1.60/5). So ON ECE the generation mean does exceed the extraction mean at all three paradigms. BUT TABLE 6 PRINTS BRIER SCORE BESIDE ECE, the paper defines BOTH as calibration measures ('The ECE and BS, are two measures of calibration that quantify the deviation from perfect calibration'), AND ON BRIER THE GRADIENT DOES NOT SURVIVE: zero-shot extraction 0.2975 (1.19/4) against generation 0.304 (1.52/5), a gap of 0.0065 and effectively nil; few-shot extraction 0.3225 (1.29/4) against generation 0.294 (1.47/5), WHICH IS REVERSED, extraction being the worse-calibrated family; fine-tuned extraction 0.375 (1.50/4) against generation 0.562 (2.81/5). ALL TWELVE MEANS ARE AGENT-DERIVED AND ARE NOT PRINTED IN THE PAPER; they are labelled derived here and must be labelled derived wherever else they are used. THE SUPPORTED STATEMENT IS THEREFORE: on src-0001's Table 6 the extraction-versus-generation calibration gradient is NOT a robust property of the data. It holds on ECE at every paradigm, vanishes on Brier at zero-shot, REVERSES on Brier at few-shot, and is large and metric-agnostic ONLY after fine-tuning, where it is driven almost entirely by two generation rows (CVE ECE 0.91 / BS 0.98 and attack vector ECE 0.87 / BS 1.00). One row shows the two metrics disagreeing outright: extraction attack vector is the BEST-calibrated extraction cell on zero-shot ECE (0.13) and the WORST on zero-shot BS (0.46). WHAT SURVIVES UNDAMAGED AND SHOULD BE CARRIED FORWARD INSTEAD: fine-tuning does not reliably improve calibration and sometimes destroys it -- ECE worsened on 7 of 9 rows and BS on the same 7. THE CONSISTENCY HALF OF THIS CANDIDATE IS UNTOUCHED: the CI widths of 0.02 (extraction) against 0.06 (generation) are a different measurement, re-verified, and stand. VERSION CHECK, NEW AT CYCLE 39: Table 6 was re-pulled WHOLE from arxiv.org/html/2503.23175v1 and all 54 cells are IDENTICAL to the cycle-25 pull from the unversioned render, which resolves to v4 (four versions exist: v1 29 Mar 2025, v2 16 Jul 2025, v3 4 Nov 2025, v4 12 Nov 2025, all 1,203 KB). The arithmetic above is therefore not version-dependent. ctr-0003 RESOLVED AT CYCLE 39.

ADDED cycle 15 by a T1 collect, status PROPOSED and deliberately not promoted -- READ THE SCOPE LIMIT BEFORE USING IT. This issue sat at score 2 from cycle 3 to cycle 15 for one reason: both candidate_resolutions above cite src-0001 and nothing else, and single-source support is a 2 by rubric. Four independent sources now measure the consistency/calibration/abstention axes on SECURITY tasks, none by src-0001's team, none on CTI material. (1) CALIBRATION: src-0013 (Siddiq/Rahman/Santos, ICSME 2026) is the first non-src-0001 source in this base reporting ECE and Brier on a security task -- GPT-4o-mini ECE 0.456-0.481, Qwen3-Coder-Next 0.408-0.421, Gemini-2.0-Flash 0.247-0.263 -- and independently reproduces src-0001's most counter-intuitive result, that an intervention meant to help can worsen calibration: moving from a controlled benchmark to a realistic repository-level setting raised ECE for every model (GPT-4o-mini 0.411->0.697, Gemini 0.161->0.721) and architectural gating helped on the controlled benchmark while degrading the realistic one. (2) INSTABILITY UNDER REPEATED IDENTICAL QUERY, src-0001's own method: src-0016 (Snyk VulnBench JS 1.0) ran each task five times with code, prompt and harness held constant and found 134/158 reference-matched findings recurred in all five runs while 80/161 unmatched findings appeared in only one of five -- a grounded-stable / volunteered-unstable split that parallels src-0001's extraction-vs-generation CI-width divide (0.02 vs 0.06). (3) PROMPT SENSITIVITY AND ABSTENTION: src-0014 (PromptAudit) fixes dataset/decoding/parsing and varies only prompting strategy, finding cross-strategy F1 ranges from 0.398 (Gemma) down to 0.103 (Mistral) and that self-consistency collapses coverage to 24.04-60.85%. (4) UNDER-REFUSAL: src-0015 (OpenSec) finds frontier IR agents over-trigger (GPT-5.2 100% containment at 82.5% FP) and locates the defect precisely -- 'the calibration gap is not in detection but in restraint' -- the same shape as src-0007's triage asymmetry. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO. It DOES establish that consistency failure, overconfidence and under-refusal are not artefacts of one team, one paper, one model family or one evaluation harness, and it supplies the base's first abstention data. It DOES NOT replicate src-0001 on CTI: every one of the four measures a security-adjacent task (secure code generation, CVE-code vulnerability detection, JavaScript SAST review, simulated incident response), NOT IoC extraction, TTP mapping, attribution or threat-report drafting. So open_question (ii) -- would the findings replicate on src-0002's and src-0005's model lists on CTI tasks -- REMAINS FULLY OPEN, and none of the four tests a model from src-0001's, src-0002's or src-0005's lists. A T4 scoring this issue must decide explicitly whether cross-domain corroboration on the same failure mode counts toward multi-source support or whether the domain gap holds it at 2; that judgement has not been made and this entry does not make it.

SCOPE RULING, made by T2 at cycle 16 and recorded here so that no future cycle re-litigates it. REASONING, three grounds. WHAT IS NEVERTHELESS ESTABLISHED, and it is not nothing: the MECHANISM -- output instability under identical or perturbed input, systematic overconfidence, and under-refusal -- is robust across four unrelated teams, four methods, four corpora and roughly fifteen models, so it is not an artefact of one paper, one team or one model family; and two of src-0001's most fragile-looking sub-findings are independently echoed by different mechanisms (an intervention intended to help WORSENING calibration: src-0013's repository-level ECE rising 0.411 to 0.697 for GPT-4o-mini and 0.161 to 0.721 for Gemini-2.0-Flash, and src-0014's adaptive-CoT reducing recall for every model, e.g. Gemma 0.420 to 0.057; and GROUNDED-OUTPUT-STABLE versus VOLUNTEERED-OUTPUT-UNSTABLE: src-0016's 134 of 158 reference-matched findings recurring in all five identical repetitions against 80 of 161 unmatched findings appearing in only one of five, paralleling src-0001's extraction-vs-generation CI widths of 0.02 vs 0.06). That is a claim about SECURITY-TASK LLM RELIABILITY GENERALLY. It is held here as context for the CTI claim, not as support for it. CONSEQUENCE FOR A T4: score this issue on its CTI candidates. A T4 may overrule this scope ruling, but if it does it must say so explicitly and give its reason -- what it must not do is silently count the four as multi-source support for a CTI claim. NO SCORE IS SET HERE; scoring is T4's work and this entry deliberately does not perform it. TWO THINGS REMAIN UNCHANGED AND SHOULD NOT BE FORGOTTEN: this base still has no non-src-0001 source measuring consistency AND calibration together, and per carry-forward [20] src-0013's and src-0014's numbers are single-pass fetches whose results tables have never been pulled whole, with src-0013 additionally carrying an unreconciled internal discrepancy (False Trust for GPT-4o-mini given as 33.9% in one section and as rising from 16.9% to 83.2% in another) -- those two figures must not be quoted together until a G2 pulls that table.

ADDED AND PROMOTED TO SUPPORTED BY CYCLE 25's T3. THE CTI-DOMAIN SINGLE-SOURCE BLOCKER IS BROKEN, BUT FOR THE CONSISTENCY HALF ONLY -- read the split below before scoring. THE CLAIM: on CTI material specifically, LLM outputs are NOT stable across repeated identical queries, and this is now measured by two teams with nothing in common. (1) src-0001 (Mezzi, Massacci, Tuma; ARES 2025, peer-reviewed -- see the cycle-25 note appended to that source, the base had wrongly carried it as an unreviewed preprint since cycle 1): 350 real threat-intelligence reports, 3 models, ten re-prompts per input with bootstrapped CIs, max CI width 0.02 for information extraction and 0.06 for information generation. The cycle-25 whole-table pull recovered the protocol sentence verbatim -- 'we re-prompt each LLM ten times on the same input, with temperature=0 and the same seed to guarantee maximum determinism' -- so the measured spread is RESIDUAL NON-DETERMINISM UNDER MAXIMAL DETERMINISM SETTINGS, which strengthens the finding. (2) src-0018 (Milenkoski and Cirstea, SentinelLabs, 9 March 2026): selective IOC/hash/playbook extraction from narrative threat reports, ground truth of 343 atomic IOCs and 1859 labeled contextual-attribute instances, five current-generation models, 'repeated executions of each evaluation experiment' under 'identical conditions', with two purpose-built decision-consistency metrics (share of IOCs receiving two or more different values for one attribute across runs; average mode-based observed disagreement). INDEPENDENCE IS CLEAN: no shared author, academia vs industry lab, different corpora, model sets a full generation apart and disjoint, and src-0018 does not cite src-0001. This clears the cycle-16 scope ruling on its own terms rather than overturning it -- src-0018 is CTI proper (IOC extraction from threat reports), not a security-adjacent task, so no cross-domain generalisation is being asserted. TWO LIMITS A T4 MUST HOLD ONTO. (a) src-0018 SUPPLIES NO NUMBERS: all four of its quantitative artefacts are images this agent cannot read, so the corroboration is of DIRECTION AND EXISTENCE only, and no magnitude may be compared with src-0001's CI widths. (b) THE CALIBRATION HALF IS UNTOUCHED: src-0018 measures ABSTENTION errors (FDR/FNR over an explicit None class), which is a restraint construct and NOT ECE/Brier -- the same non-pooling rule already recorded for src-0015. Proper-scoring calibration on CTI remains src-0001-only, gpt4o-only, nine table rows. SO THE HONEST SCORING POSITION IS SPLIT: consistency-on-CTI is now two-source and qualitative-plus-quantitative; calibration-on-CTI is still one-source. This issue's title asks both. === REWRITTEN AT CYCLE 39 TO RESOLVE ctr-0005, WHICH FOUND LIMIT (a) ABOVE TOO BROAD. Limit (a) as written -- 'src-0018 SUPPLIES NO NUMBERS: all four of its quantitative artefacts are images' -- is WITHDRAWN AND REPLACED, on two counts. FIRST, THE COUNT IS WRONG: the page carries TEN figures, of which six are quantitative, not four; the two no cycle knew existed are 'Prediction and error diversity (GPT-4.1 and Claude Sonnet 4.5)' and 'LLM Performance in Playbook and knowledge graph assembly', plus 'Human vs. LLMs: Time efficiency in report processing'. SECOND, THE PROHIBITION WAS SCOPED TO THE WHOLE PAGE WHEN IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN SCOPED TO THE PERFORMANCE ARTEFACTS. THE CORRECTED SCOPE, AND IT IS THE OPERATIVE RULE FROM CYCLE 39 ONWARD: the FOUR performance artefacts -- the 'LLM decision consistency' table and the 'Abstention error rates', 'Selective IOC extraction performance' and 'Value assignment performance' charts -- are confirmed IMAGE, CANNOT READ, for a THIRD independent time, and quoting, estimating, ranking or comparing THOSE magnitudes REMAINS FORBIDDEN IN FULL; no cycle should re-attempt them by fetch, since three have failed and no OCR route exists in this sandbox. THIS STRENGTHENS THE CANDIDATE RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT: two independent teams, on disjoint model sets a generation apart, on different CTI corpora, both report output instability on CTI extraction tasks AT TEMPERATURE 0. The corroboration is still of DIRECTION AND EXISTENCE only -- no magnitude may be compared with src-0001's CI widths -- but it is now direction-and-existence under a matched and unusually strong experimental control, which is a stronger form of agreement than two uncontrolled observations. RULING ON ctr-0005 STEP (ii), THE 41-MINUTE HUMAN BASELINE: IT DOES NOT BELONG IN THIS ISSUE AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT ENTERED HERE.
